einzeiler: The early life and perilous adventures of mountain man Jim Bridger on the American…
kurzfassung: Orphaned at a young age, Jim Bridger joined Ashley's Hundred in 1822 and plunged into the dangerous American frontier. He survived intense conflicts with Native American tribes, explored the Great Salt Lake, and endured a severe arrow wound. His trailblazing exploits cemented his legacy as one of the most famous mountain men of the West.
stichpunkte: Jim Bridger lost both parents and his brother within two years, becoming an orphan at age 13.
He learned survival and trade skills while working as a flatboatman and gunsmith apprentice.
In 1822, Bridger joined William Ashley and Andrew Henry's trapping expedition up the Missouri River.
He survived the deadly Arikara attack in 1823, which forced trappers to abandon river travel for overland routes.
Bridger became the first Euro-American to reach and identify the Great Salt Lake in 1824.
He survived the Battle of Pierre's Hole, the largest engagement between trappers and Native Americans.
Bridger was severely wounded by Blackfoot arrows during a clash on the Gallatin River.
An iron arrowhead remained lodged in Bridger's back for three years until doctor Marcus Whitman removed it.
beschreibung:
In 1822, eighteen-year-old Jim Bridger joins the Ashley-Henry fur company and travels up the Missouri River to trap beaver in the West. But before he learns the basics of trapping, Arikara warriors attack the company. And then a grizzly bear attacks Bridger’s friend, Hugh Glass. In the years following the attack, Bridger becomes the first American to taste the waters of the Great Salt Lake and he helps organize the first Mountain Man Rendezvous.
